name: LeetSwap WETH/AIBASE pair fee-transfer drain
summary: LeetSwapV2Pair exposed its fee-transfer helper publicly without caller, token, or amount authorization. An unprivileged caller could move a pair's counterpart-token balance into its fees contract, synchronize the depleted reserve, and drain WETH through the resulting reserve distortion.
notes: LeetSwap factory CREATE2 deployment of this immutable-bearing pair runtime. Archival code is absent in block 2010798 and hashes to 0x59286f53eb62798a994834130fd7ee5bb8faa04dd70c685059d65e9f65128632 at deployment and immediately before the incident; the pair has no proxy code-selection path.

The pair sent 12.288366714968444785 WETH to the attack helper. Excluding the helper's identifiable 0.001 WETH setup-swap input leaves exact pre-recovery victim depletion of 12.287366714968444785 WETH, valued at DefiLlama's nearest observation of $1,862.36. The public fee-transfer call also moved the counterpart token into the pair's fees contract; that internal transfer is excluded because claim allocation and recoverability cannot be isolated from the receipts, so no speculative counterpart-token value is assigned.
This pair-specific record is part of a coordinated same-attacker LeetSwap umbrella. Loss is partitioned by pair deployment and is not duplicated across sibling records.
